narratives.name: Partner Technical Capability Development
narratives.description: The progression from assessed capability gaps to scaled, independent technical capability across TDP areas.

narrativeContexts.context: Partner technical capability in the TEP context goes beyond individual certifications to encompass the organizational capacity to independently sell, deliver, and support Red Hat-based solutions across specific TDP areas.

The TDP adoption lifecycle represents a partner's progressive evolution from acceptance of a technology area through first customer win to sustained, independent achievement, tracked through whitespace map maturity assessments and initiative outcomes.

Capability maturity is evidenced through whitespace map progression, completed initiative milestones, validated solution briefs, and customer engagement outcomes documented in the TEP quarterly review cycle.

Partners reaching the Scaling state demonstrate the Ecosystem Success Pathway aspiration where they sell Red Hat technology independently, requiring progressively less Red Hat overhead for ongoing success.

narratives.name: Technical Engagement Plan Lifecycle
narratives.description: The lifecycle of the TEP artifact from creation in RHSC through multi-quarter optimization.

narrativeContexts.context: The Technical Engagement Plan is the primary planning artifact owned by the Ecosystem Solutions Architect, created in Red Hat Sales Cloud to operationalize the technical dimension of a partner engagement as the complement to the Partner Account Manager's Partner Success Plan.

Each TEP comprises three structural components: a Scorecard capturing strategic technical sales information and quarterly objectives, a Whitespace Map providing visual capability assessment across product lines, and an Initiatives section with linked 15-action execution frameworks targeting specific Technical Decision Points.

The evolution from Google Doc templates to RHSC-native plans enables structured data capture, initiative tracking, and management reporting through the PSP/TEP dashboard, transforming TEP execution from anecdotal partner updates to data-driven portfolio management.
TEP maturity is demonstrated when multi-quarter data produces portfolio-level insights that inform strategic investment decisions about which partners and TDP areas receive engagement resources.

narratives.name: Technical Engagement Planning Intent
narratives.description: The narrative arc for how ESAs drive partner technical capability through structured engagement planning.

narrativeContexts.context: Partner organizations commit to Red Hat technology partnerships but lack structured technical engagement plans that translate business strategy into actionable technical roadmaps, resulting in ad hoc capability development and inconsistent partner outcomes across the portfolio.

Ecosystem Solutions Architects must create structured Technical Engagement Plans in Red Hat Sales Cloud that operationalize Partner Success Plan objectives through targeted initiatives, each driving a partner toward sustained, independent technical capability in specific technology areas.

ESAs create TEPs with AI-assisted content generation, populate scorecard and whitespace assessments, derive initiatives aligned to TDP focus areas, and execute a standardized 15-action framework progressing partners from acceptance through discovery, solution co-creation, commercial alignment, and operational readiness.

Partners achieve sustained, independent capability to drive Red Hat revenue through specific technology areas, evidenced by completed customer engagements, productized solutions, and progressively decreasing Red Hat involvement in ongoing partner success.

narratives.name: TEP Initiative Execution Lifecycle
narratives.description: The 15-action lifecycle from initiative definition through TDP achievement.

narrativeContexts.context: The TEP Initiative is the core operational unit through which Technical Engagement Plans are executed, each scoped to a single Technical Decision Point and product line with a standardized 15-action framework progressing the partner from acceptance through sustained achievement.

The initiative lifecycle embodies the partner TDP adoption journey: acceptance, discovery and design, technical win, GTM readiness, and sustained achievement where the partner independently sells Red Hat technology with progressively less Red Hat involvement.

Each of the 15 ESA-prefixed actions provides a trackable milestone visible in the management dashboard, enabling quantitative progress assessment against SMART objectives with leading and lagging indicators agreed with partner stakeholders.

A completed initiative represents a partner that can independently engage customers in a specific TDP technology area, requiring progressively less Red Hat involvement and contributing to the broader ecosystem self-sufficiency objective.
